t: The funds authorized to be appropriated in section 6(e) of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, as amended (33 U.S.C. 466 et seq.), for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1971, shall remain available until October 31, 1971.

fable.w: This section only extends the period of availability for funds authorized under the Federal Water Pollution Control Act. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government; there is no tempting participation reading beyond the reference to a regulatory statute.

opus.w: This provision only extends how long funds authorized under section 6(e) of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act remain available. It involves no outside party: no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. The citation to an environmental statute that has participatory features elsewhere does not bring any participation into this section.
opus.b: **Tempting reading:** The section cites the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, which has consultation provisions elsewhere, so it might seem to involve outside parties. That reading fails here. This section only extends how long already-authorized funds stay available. No one outside the federal government consults on, comments on, or challenges any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section solely addresses the duration for which appropriated funds remain available. It does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with parties outside the federal government, such as the public, states, or experts. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: The funds authorized to be appropriated in section 6(e) of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, as amended (33 U.S.C. 466 et seq.), for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1971, shall remain available until October 31, 1971.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are for the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, which often involves public participation, this section implies participation. However, this specific text only deals with the availability period of appropriated funds. It does not mention any consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory body involving non-federal parties.
